reference: Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 coupe, 6th generation, 2017-2024 (engineering reference only; the game car gets a fictional name)

tag_legend.F: manufacturer figure (GM press material, product guide or GM service bulletin)
tag_legend.P: published spec from a third party (spec site, Wikipedia, enthusiast press, parts makers)
tag_legend.M: measured in a test (magazine instrumented test, dyno sheet)
tag_legend.E: estimate made here; the note says how

model_years.note: 6th-gen production ended 14 Dec 2023; 2024 was the last model year.

drive_side.note: US market. A right-hand-drive conversion was sold in Australia/NZ (GMSV); not researched.

launch_rating_history.value: Announced at an estimated 640 hp / 640 lb-ft; SAE-certified at 650 hp / 650 lb-ft in Aug 2016 before sales
launch_rating_history.note: Explains why some GM documents still give 868 Nm (= 640 lb-ft).

model_year_changes.value: 2017 launch (manual or 10-speed auto; coupe and convertible). 2018 adds ZL1 1LE (manual only). 2019 refresh: new rear fascia and dual-element taillamps, 8-in infotainment; ZL1 1LE gets the 10L90 from Feb 2019; GM lists length 190.2 in for 2019 vs 188.3 in for 2017. 2024: final year (Collector's Edition; Garage 56 Edition of 56 cars, 1LE-based).
model_year_changes.note: 2020-2023 changes were small and were not researched in detail.

convertible_differences.value: Heavier (4,113 lb manual / 4,148 lb automatic vs 3,883 / 3,944 lb coupe); automatic convertible uses a 2.77 final drive instead of 2.85; reported to lack the eLSD.
convertible_differences.note: Weights are GM (F). The 2.77 ratio and the missing eLSD come only from an Autoblog first-drive snippet (P); not confirmed in a GM document.

variant_1LE.value: ZL1 1LE Extreme Track Performance Package (2018-2024): Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers (23 lb lighter than Magnetic Ride, hard-mounted), springs about 4x stiffer, solid subframe mounts, adjustable camber plates, threaded front spring perch (+/-10 mm), 3-position rear anti-roll bar (+15% / -10%), 19x11 / 19x12 forged wheels with Goodyear Eagle F1 Supercar 3R 305/30ZR19 / 325/30ZR19, carbon rear wing (300 lb downforce at 150 mph), front splitter and dive planes, about 60 lb lighter (3,820 lb est.), 1.10 g. Manual only for 2018; 10L90 from Feb 2019. Nurburgring 7:16.04 (2017), 13.6 s faster than the standard ZL1.
variant_1LE.note: '4x stiffer springs' is from Wikipedia citing Car and Driver (P).

layout.note: Bank angle from the Corvette Z06 LT4 overview (same engine family).

crank_type.note: Forged steel crank is stated for the LT4. 'Cross-plane' is deduced: the even-firing 1-8-7-2-6-5-4-3 order needs it, and every GM small-block V8 uses one.

compression_ratio.note: Some spec databases list 11.5:1 (that is the naturally aspirated LT1); ignore.

valvetrain.value: OHV pushrod, 2 valves per cylinder, hydraulic roller lifters, single cam-in-block with dual-equal VVT (vane phaser)

valves.value: intake 54 mm (2.13 in) titanium; exhaust 40.4 mm (1.59 in) hollow sodium-filled; rocker ratio 1.8
valves.note: Corvette Z06 LT4 data; assumed shared with the Camaro LT4.

camshaft.value: lift 0.492 / 0.551 in (int/exh); duration at 0.050 in 189 / 223 deg; lobe separation 120 deg

lubrication.note: The Corvette Z06 LT4 is dry-sump; the Camaro is not.

cylinder_deactivation.value: not confirmed for the Camaro ZL1
cylinder_deactivation.note: The Z06 LT4 has Active Fuel Management; not verified for the Camaro.

max_torque.note: 650 lb-ft (SAE certified) at 3,600 rpm. GM's 2019 product guide prints 868 Nm, which is the pre-certification 640 lb-ft.

torque_landmarks.value: 457 lb-ft (620 Nm) just off idle; 625 lb-ft (847 Nm) by 2,800 rpm; 90% of peak (585 lb-ft, 793 Nm) from 2,500 to 5,400 rpm
torque_landmarks.note: EngineLabs quoting GM's launch material for the Z06 LT4.

torque_curve_wheel_measured.unit: rpm, Nm at the rear wheels
torque_curve_wheel_measured.note: READ FROM A CHART: blue 'stock' trace of K&N's Dynojet sheet, stock 2017 ZL1 (8,620 mi), 4th gear, SAE correction (CF 1.02), smoothing 5. Digitised by pixel colour every 250 rpm, cross-checked against the power trace (hp = lb-ft x rpm / 5252 agrees within 1%). Transmission type not stated. The run starts at 2,000 rpm. Peak about 562 lb-ft (762 Nm) at 3,300-3,500 rpm and about 546 whp at 6,100 rpm. The drop above 6,100 rpm is real in the chart but conflicts with GM's 650 hp at 6,400 (likely heat soak or calibration on the dyno).

torque_curve_crank_estimate.note: Built through GM's points (881 Nm at 3,600; 723 Nm at 6,400 = 485 kW; 620 Nm just off idle, put at 1,000 rpm; 847 Nm by 2,800; >= 793 Nm from 2,500 to 5,400), with the mid-range shape taken from the K&N wheel curve. Wheel/crank ratio comes out 0.82-0.90 between 2,500 and 6,000 rpm. Use this for the simulation.

redline.note: Tachometer redline quoted in an Australian review (manual car). Matches the supercharger's 20,150 rpm limit at a 3.10 drive ratio.

max_engine_speed.note: GM's crate-engine page gives 6,600 rpm max recommended speed (read via search snippet).

rev_limiter.note: Fuel-cut limiter assumed at the 6,600 rpm max speed; hysteresis about 100-150 rpm (E). Exact factory limiter behaviour not found.

idle_rpm.note: Not found. Typical warm idle for Gen V LT V8s is about 600-700 rpm; cold start flares to about 1,000-1,200 rpm (E).

launch_control.value: Custom Launch Control: driver-set launch rpm, wheel-slip target 5-15%, surface type; works in Track mode with PTM. 1LE automatic bulletin: rpm adjustable down to 800, GM recommends at least 1,200 rpm.
launch_control.note: Default launch rpm not published. Suggested simulation hold: about 2,500-3,000 rpm for the automatic, 3,500-4,000 rpm for the manual (E).

firing_order.note: Same order as Gen III/IV LS and Gen V LT V8s.

cylinder_numbering.value: GM convention: cylinders numbered front to back; odd 1-3-5-7 on the left (driver's, US LHD) bank, even 2-4-6-8 on the right bank; No. 1 is the front cylinder of the left bank

per_bank_firing_intervals.value: left bank (1,7,5,3) and right bank (8,2,6,4) each fire at 180-270-180-90 crank-degree intervals (rotated); the whole engine fires evenly every 90 deg
per_bank_firing_intervals.note: Derived from the firing order and cross-plane crank. This uneven per-bank train is the source of the V8 burble.

firing_frequency.value: rpm / 15 (4 firings per crank revolution): 43 Hz at 650 rpm, 200 Hz at 3,000 rpm, 433 Hz at 6,500 rpm

heat_exchangers.note: Track cooling: radiator with dual auxiliary radiators, engine oil, transmission and differential coolers, intercooler circuit.

model.note: Confirms the starting fact. GM bulletin calls it an Eaton supercharger with a new Camaro-specific lid.

displacement.note: Usually quoted as 1.7 L; the model number means 1,740 cc.

rotor_type.value: twin-rotor Roots type, 4 lobes on each rotor, 160-degree helical twist

max_rotor_speed.note: = 6,500 engine rpm x 3.10. Corvette Action Center rounds it to 20,000 rpm.

max_boost.note: 65 kPa gauge. Corvette Action Center gives 9.71 psi (0.67 bar). GM's Z06 launch material used 9.4 psi.

intercooler.value: air-to-liquid, two 'bricks' inside the supercharger case, on a separate low-temperature coolant circuit with its own pump and a heat exchanger ahead of the radiator; up to 60 C (140 F) charge cooling
intercooler.note: Camaro-specific: a new lid lets the bricks sit higher for better airflow (GM 17-NA-251, F).

whine_fundamental.value: 8 pulses per rotor revolution (4 lobes x 2 rotors): f = rpm x 3.10 x 8 / 60 = 0.4133 x engine rpm
whine_fundamental.note: Standard Roots-blower relation (a 2-lobe blower gives 4 pulses per revolution). The single-rotor lobe-pass line (4 per rev, half this frequency) may also be audible. The whine sits at 6.2x the firing frequency (engine order 24.8), so it never locks to the engine's harmonics, which is why it stands out. Timing-gear mesh whine is also possible; tooth count unknown.

whine_table.unit: engine rpm, rotor rpm, 4x lobe-pass Hz, 8x pulse Hz

whine_character.value: Prominent at low revs and part throttle, a 'characterful' whine under the exhaust; masked by exhaust noise at high revs and by wind with the convertible roof down above about 75 mph

main_spec.note: Co-developed with Ford. GM bulletin 19-NA-038 and NHTSA listings for 2017-2018 ZL1 use RPO MGL; one secondary source says MX0.

gear_ratios_10L90.note: Overall spread 7.39. Cross-check: 1,859 rpm at 80 mph in 10th by calculation vs C/D's 'less than 1900 rpm'.

final_drive_auto_convertible.note: Also listed on press-style spec sheets per search snippets.

torque_converter.value: 260 mm, integral turbine clutch, lock-up clutch with electronically controlled capacity clutch (ECCC) slip control

converter_stall_rpm.note: Not published. Estimate for a 260 mm converter behind 881 Nm.

clutches.value: 6 (4 rotating, 2 brake) incl. a triple-clutch assembly

shift_times.value: GM: 1-2 upshift 36% quicker, 2-3 27% quicker, 3-4 26% quicker than Porsche's PDK; no absolute times published

shift_time_sim.note: Suggested torque-interruption time for the simulation; secondary press quoted 'about 100 ms' (unverified).

shift_logic.value: Sport/Track: holds gears in hard driving, holds gear after a sudden lift until near redline, downshifts under braking keeping above about 3,000 rpm, upshifts one gear at a time back to 10th when cruising. 1LE auto Track pattern: upshifts about 3,000 rpm and downshifts about 2,000 rpm in normal driving; rev-matches all downshifts.
shift_logic.note: Bulletin is for the 2019 ZL1 1LE automatic; the Sport-mode behaviour is described generally.

speed_per_gear_6500rpm_auto_kmh.note: Rear tyre 305/30ZR20 (691 mm), rolling radius 0.335 m (3% under static, E). 1st ends near 38 mph; 2nd ends at 60-61 mph (6,500-6,600 rpm), so 0-60 mph needs exactly one upshift.

top_speed_gear.note: The Drive: the car never needs more than 8th; calculation agrees.

manual_variant.value: TREMEC TR-6060 6-speed manual (RPO MH3) with Active Rev Match

gear_ratios_manual.note: Bulletin is for the 2018 ZL1 1LE (MH3). Also fits the 2017 ZL1 manual: '60 mph in first' (The Drive) and about 100 km/h in 1st at 6,500 rpm (WhichCar) both match 2.29 x 3.73.

speed_per_gear_6500rpm_manual_kmh.note: Same tyre assumptions; 6th is drag-limited (about 6,400 rpm at 198 mph).

differential.value: Electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD), 226 mm ring gear, hydraulically actuated clutch pack
differential.note: Bulletin text is for the 1LE; it says the 1LE eLSD differs only in calibration.

elsd_capacity.value: 0-200 Nm breakaway torque between the rear wheels, infinitely variable
elsd_capacity.note: GM's wording; treat as clutch preload/locking capacity.

elsd_modes.value: Mode 1 stability (default, PTM Wet); Mode 2 TCS and StabiliTrak off (more turn-in, exit traction); Mode 3 PTM Dry/Sport 1/Sport 2/Race; Mode 4 TCS off, StabiliTrak on

traction_system.value: Performance Traction Management, 5 modes: Wet, Dry, Sport 1, Sport 2, Race; StabiliTrak; Competitive Driving Mode; Line Lock

sim_suggestion.note: Clutch-type approximation of the eLSD for the game's differential model (GM's range is 0-200 Nm); tune in testing.

curb_coupe_auto.note: 3,944 lb; GM curb weight (US convention: full fluids, no driver).

measured_coupe_auto.note: 3,933 lb, Car and Driver test car (read from a search snippet; C/D blocks this agent).

weight_distribution_front.note: Not found. Estimate for a front-engined supercharged V8 coupe with 11 heat exchangers up front; the 6th-gen Camaro SS is usually quoted near 52/48. Verify.

sim_mass.note: Coupe automatic curb weight plus a 75 kg driver, as for the GT12 prototype.

length.note: 190.2 in for 2019+. Wikipedia gives 4,783 mm (188.3 in) for 2017-18.

height.note: 52.4 in. Wikipedia lists 53.1 in generally and 52.0 in for the 1LE.

front_overhang.note: From the side-view photo's front/rear overhang ratio (190:220 px) applied to length minus wheelbase (2,001 mm).

ground_clearance.note: Not published. About 110-125 mm under the front splitter, about 130 mm at the sills, from the photo scaled by wheel diameter.

frontal_area.note: 0.85 x width x height. A lap-simulation site uses 2.07 m^2.

front_tyre.note: Goodyear Eagle F1 Supercar 3, Camaro-specific compound and construction. Diameter 679 mm (calc).

rear_tyre.note: Goodyear Eagle F1 Supercar 3. Diameter 691 mm (calc).

1LE_tyres.value: 305/30ZR19 front, 325/30ZR19 rear, Goodyear Eagle F1 Supercar 3R
1LE_tyres.note: Footprint about 10% larger than the ZL1; 1.5 kg lighter per corner.

1LE_wheels.value: 19 x 11 in front, 19 x 12 in rear forged aluminium

summer_tyre_note.value: summer-only tyres; do not use below -7 C (20 F)

track_pressures_1LE.value: cold 26 psi (180 kPa), hot target 32-35 psi; 44 psi for sustained high speed
track_pressures_1LE.note: GM ran 44 psi in the 198 mph test (THEDRIVE_198).

front.value: Brembo six-piston monobloc fixed calipers; 390 x 36 mm two-piece vented rotors
front.note: 15.35 in. Rotor thickness from the 1LE bulletin.

rear.value: Brembo four-piston fixed calipers; 365 x 28 mm vented rotors (one-piece)

factory_60_0.note: 107 ft. GM's guide misprints the metric value as 35 m.

cd_70_0.note: 143 ft, C/D March 2017 automatic coupe (search snippet).

mt_60_0_1LE.note: 91 ft, ZL1 1LE, Motor Trend Best Driver's Car 2017 (via a mirror of MT's data).

sim_suggestion.note: Enough to lock the wheels at 1,864 kg; tune so 100-0 km/h is about 33-35 m.

drag_coefficient.note: GM has never published a Cd for the 6th-gen ZL1. A lap-simulation site uses 0.364 (with 2.07 m^2).

drag_area_topspeed_fit.note: Fitted so 650 hp gives 198 mph in 8th (~6,100 rpm, ~480 kW): 85-90% driveline efficiency, Crr 0.012-0.016, air 1.20-1.225 kg/m^3 give CdA 0.90-0.99. It absorbs heat soak and high-speed tyre losses. The lap-sim value (0.75) would let the car reach about 210 mph.

lift_standard_ZL1.value: GM says the package reduces lift with no significant drag penalty (pedestal 'stanchion' spoiler, patent-pending auxiliary transmission cooler); no numbers
lift_standard_ZL1.note: Suggest near-zero net lift (ClA about 0 front, 0.05 rear) for the simulation (E).

downforce_1LE.note: 300 lb (136 kg) at 150 mph from the carbon wing; equals ClA of about 0.48 m^2 at the rear (E).

wind_tunnel.value: more than 100 hours in two wind tunnels plus CFD

front_suspension.value: MacPherson-type strut with dual lower ball joints, monotube struts, direct-acting stabilizer bar, Magnetic Ride Control

rear_suspension.value: independent five-link, monotube Magnetic Ride Control shocks, direct-acting stabilizer bar

spring_rates.note: Not published. 1LE springs are about 4x the ZL1's (P).

track_alignment.value: front camber -2.7 deg, caster 7.9 deg, toe 0.1 deg total; rear camber -2.0 deg, toe 0.1 deg total
track_alignment.note: GM track alignment for ZL1/1LE; street alignment not found.

ride_height.note: Not published. 1LE front ride height adjustable +/-10 mm.

steering_type.value: ZF rack-mounted electric power steering, variable ratio

steering_ratio.note: Not found. Typical for the platform about 12-14:1 variable; about 2.4 turns lock-to-lock (E, unverified).

max_road_wheel_angle.note: From the 11.7 m kerb-to-kerb turning circle, 2,811 mm wheelbase and 1,610 mm track.

magnetic_ride_weight.value: the 1LE's DSSV dampers are 23 lb (10.4 kg) lighter than the ZL1's Magnetic Ride set

factory_top_speed.note: 198 mph, two-way average at Papenburg (Germany), 10-speed car, stock apart from 44 psi tyres; 202.3 mph one way with the wind, 193.3 mph against.

factory_0_100kmh.note: Not published by GM; 0-60 mph plus about 0.15 s.

nurburgring.value: ZL1 about 7:29.6 (13.6 s slower than the 1LE); ZL1 1LE 7:16.04 (2017, GM test, driver Bill Wise)

value.how_read: 0-60/quarter from the 0-60specs aggregator; braking, skidpad, 50-70 and weight from search snippets of the Yahoo-syndicated C/D test
search snippet of the Yahoo-syndicated C/D test; C/D notes the manual is 0.3 s slower to 60 than the auto
The Drive article on the video
0-60specs aggregator plus a search snippet of MT's BDC data

magazine_tests.note: Car and Driver and Motor Trend block this agent, so their full data boxes (0-100, 0-130, 5-60, sound) could not be read.

simulation_targets.note: 0-100 km/h is E; 0-100 mph is M (Hennessey).

exhaust_manifolds.value: Tri-Y design exhaust manifolds, 'improves torque production and sound quality'
exhaust_manifolds.note: Z06 LT4 manifolds are cast austenitic stainless steel (P, CAC_Z06_LT4); Camaro material not confirmed.

catalysts.note: Stated for the Z06 LT4; assumed for the Camaro. Count and position not confirmed.

crossover.note: X-pipe vs H-pipe vs none NOT confirmed for the factory ZL1 system. Gap.

mufflers_and_valves.value: dual-mode 'NPP' exhaust: electronically actuated butterfly valves let exhaust bypass the rear mufflers; valves open on demand and always in Track mode
mufflers_and_valves.note: NPP exhaust standard on the 1LE with larger bell-shaped tips (F).

tips.value: quad tips: two per side at the outer corners of the rear diffuser (split rear exit)
tips.note: Seen in a Commons photo; Borla calls the stock exit 'dual split rear', Flowmaster 'factory quad NPP'.

modes.value: Stealth (quietest, valves closed), Tour, Sport, Track (valves open)
modes.note: Mode names from enthusiast sources; GM documents confirm Sport and Track. Exact valve map per mode not found.

overrun_and_wot_pops.value: 'Pop' or 'backfire' sounds during wide-open-throttle maneuvers in Sport or Track mode are normal; they go away in other modes
overrun_and_wot_pops.note: GM bulletin 17-NA-078, March 2017, 2015-2017 Camaro and Corvette LT4. Reviewers also mention 'exhaust blatting on the overrun'.

limiter_behaviour.value: not documented; assume fuel cut at about 6,600 rpm with a fast bounce

shift_sound.value: 10-speed upshifts are very fast with a brief torque dip; 1LE auto rev-matches every downshift

launch_sound_note.value: GM: a launch setting below 1,200 rpm 'will produce an unpleasant sound'

cd_interior_dba.note: NOT OBTAINED: Car and Driver's idle / full-throttle / 70 mph figures could not be read (site blocks this agent). Gap.

proxy_interior_db_previous_gen.note: 2013 Camaro ZL1 convertible (previous generation, supercharged LSA 6.2), Edmunds, Sept 2012. Proxy only.

estimated_interior_dba.note: From the previous-gen proxy, adjusted for a coupe with a louder valved exhaust. Replace with C/D data when available.

exterior_levels.note: No published pass-by or exterior figures found.

value.quote: Crank it up, and it sounds hellacious, giving you an auditory taste of the performance potential that lies within.
it also does a good job of shutting up when you want it to.
It's so loud you can't even hear the supercharger whine.
value.context: convertible, roof down, above about 75 mph

value.quote: it's the whine of the supercharger that dominates at low revs
the angry, hard-edged growl of the 6.2-litre V8
just a bit of burble reaching your ears, as well as a faint whine from the supercharger

value.type: onboard POV, hard pulls and supercharger sound
flyby, stock exhaust, full/partial throttle and revs (2018 ZL1)
cold start and revs with burbles (2018 ZL1)
cold start and acceleration, stock per description (2023 ZL1)

reference_videos.note: Links only, not downloaded. Stock status is from titles and descriptions; check before use.

value.what: Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing: LT4 6.2 supercharged V8 (same engine family, own calibration) with an aftermarket AWE SwitchPath exhaust; start-up, revs, acceleration; 301 s, Opus 48 kHz stereo
value.author: Drag Racing Wheels - Forgestar - Weld - Race Stars (YouTube)

value.what: Chevrolet Corvette C6 ZR1 (LS9 6.2 supercharged V8, Eaton TVS R2300 with 4-lobe rotors) pulling away at Goodwood Festival of Speed 2010; 12 s, Vorbis 44.1 kHz stereo
value.author: Ed Pond (Wikimedia user Edvvc)

free_recordings.note: No freely licensed recording of a Camaro ZL1 itself was found on Wikimedia Commons; archive.org items found were unlicensed YouTube copies. Attribution notes are in the audio folder's LICENSES.txt. Check the licences suit a Roblox game before use (BY needs attribution; BY-SA also needs share-alike for derivatives).

body_style.value: long-hood, short-deck 2+2 fastback coupe with a high beltline and a low, narrow greenhouse; wide front fenders with vents; big lower grille, carbon hood vent, front splitter; integrated rear spoiler

engine_position.value: front-engined, longitudinal, much of the V8 behind the front axle line
engine_position.note: Typical of the Alpha platform; not measured.

front_axle_x.unit: fraction of length from the front
front_axle_x.note: Front overhang about 925 mm of 4,812 mm.

windscreen_base_x.unit: fraction of length from the front
windscreen_base_x.note: Cowl at the body side about 710 mm behind the front wheel centre (photo scaled by the wheelbase).

windscreen_top_x.unit: fraction of length from the front
windscreen_top_x.note: Roof header; photo is a convertible with the top up.

roof_peak_x.unit: fraction of length from the front
roof_peak_x.note: Range 0.55-0.60; above the front seat backs.

rear_window_base_x.unit: fraction of length from the front
rear_window_base_x.note: Where the backlight meets the deck.

rear_axle_x.unit: fraction of length from the front

beltline_height.note: Side-window bottom edge; daylight opening only about 370 mm tall.

nose.value: blunt, near-vertical fascia; hood falls from about 930 mm at the cowl to about 770 mm at the leading edge; splitter about 110-125 mm off the ground

tail.value: short, high deck (about 1,040 mm at the spoiler lip), near-vertical tail panel with wide horizontal lamps, diffuser with two pairs of tips at the corners

photo_caveat.value: No clean coupe side profile with a free licence was found. Proportions come from a near-side view of a modified convertible (aftermarket wing, decals); perspective shortens the ends, so lengths were scaled from the wheelbase and the published length rather than from end points.
